validity_notes: INFRASTRUCTURE FAILURE: No LLM API keys are available in the execution environment. The frozen decision_rule C1-C4 requires real LLM API calls and cannot be evaluated. This is explicitly documented in request.json:inherited_last_verdict.
Per the packet contract (research/EXPERIMENT_PACKET.md section 9), infrastructure failure is NOT a scientific negative. No evidence was produced or falsified.

The frozen decision_rule states: 'MEASUREMENT_INVALID if API failures prevent completion of >=5 tasks.' Since 0/32 tasks executed, this threshold is met (0 >= 5 is false, but the actual condition is that API failures prevent ALL execution).

The parent analytical ceiling (5.42% token savings on synthetic 32-task corpus) remains the most recent valid measurement. COLD 77 tokens/task is analytical (tiktoken counting), not from real LLM execution.

Key validity gaps carried forward from parent: (i) C1 success rate assumed 100% not measured, (ii) completion tokens estimated not measured, (iii) browser/verification costs omitted, (iv) COLD baseline viability (success rate) entirely unmeasured with real LLM.

Representation loss: The analytical tiktoken measurement (EXP-PRODUCT-35330741529) measures prompt tokens accurately but estimates completion tokens. Real LLM execution could reveal different completion token counts and potentially different success rates.

No code modifications were made to src/spider/kernel.py or any registry-authorized code root. The product lane's allowed_code_roots (src, tests, sdk, pyproject.toml) were not modified because the experiment could not execute.

This result preserves the chain: RAW EVIDENCE (no API keys) -> OBSERVATION (0/32 tasks executed) -> DERIVED MEASUREMENT (none possible) -> INTERPRETATION (infrastructure failure, not scientific negative).
